title: A pond in the lab, and nothing in the world can go in it
question: This is a pond placed in the lab bed -- stone-lined basin, 152 wide and 28 deep -- at frames 6k, 20k, 60k and 90k. It holds perfectly: 4,256 water cells, exactly constant, and it costs nothing (0.012 ms/tick against 0.012 for the same basin left dry). The bed around it thrives. Nothing ever enters it. Before I write the build order: is this the bed you want aquatic work proved in, and is a pond this size right -- or do you want something wider and shallower, a shoreline rather than a tank?
context_md:
**The pond needed no engine change at all.** The research said a basin would have to be a `LabBox` field; it does not -- `Placement::Fill` already takes `"water"`, so this is a scenario file (`the_pond.ron`) and nothing else. That is a correction to my own report.

**What the second image is for.** The same bed with the water left out. At one seed the colony does *better* in the dry pit than in the wet one or on a flat bed (28 ants against 4 and 3 at frame 90,000) -- so a pond as a bare *barrier* buys nothing, and the dry pit is the outlier, probably as shelter. A seed sweep is running now. The point for the plan: **water only becomes interesting when there is something to eat in it**, which is the research's own conclusion arriving from a different direction.

items.label: the pond, stocked
items.caption: Frames 6k / 20k / 60k / 90k. The pond holds its level exactly. Plants crowd both banks. The water stays empty.

items.label: same bed, no water
items.caption: The identical bed with the basin left dry -- the control that says what the water itself is worth.
